parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated key (e.g. a UUID v4) that makes a retried act request safe (ADR 0030). Required on every POST: the key store is wired in every runtime mode, and a request without the header is a 400 idempotency-key-required. Reuse the SAME key for retries of one logical submit (same body): the first answer is stored for 24 hours and replayed byte for byte with Idempotency-Replayed: true, without running the act again, whenever that answer is final for the request — a success; a refusal of the request itself (400, 410, 413, 415, and the 409 that the confirmation token was already used); and, because an approval spends its single-use token before it delegates, a peer refusal that arrived after that spend (409 no pending work to release, 409 the move was rejected on a domain rule, 404 the path or the assignment is unknown): these are replayed under the same key, never re-sent with a new one. A refusal that only reflects the peers' state at the time — 409 the release is not currently recommended, 409 evidence incomplete, 409 the target path is not understaffed, 409 no reallocation move — stores nothing and releases the key (ADR 0033): retry the SAME key once the state changed; a different body under a released key is a new request, not a conflict. Use a NEW key for each new submit. Reusing a key with a different method, path or body is a 409 idempotency-key-reused. A key that is not 1-128 printable ASCII characters starting and ending with a visible character is a 400 idempotency-key-invalid. The pattern describes the header as sent on the wire: the key, optionally followed by spaces or tabs, which are HTTP optional whitespace that the HTTP stack drops before the service reads the value (RFC 9110 section 5.5), so they are never part of the key. A 5xx answer is never stored, so its retry runs again; the single-use confirmation token still allows at most one delegation (ADR 0027).
